question: What penalties can the stewards impose on a driver involved in an incident during a race under the 2026 F1 regulations?
reference: Five-second or ten-second time penalty, a drive-through penalty, and a stop-and-go style penalty (Article B1.9.5).

question: When will the stewards decide not to penalise a driver involved in an incident?
reference: Unless it is clear that a driver was wholly or predominantly to blame for the incident, no penalty is imposed (the stewards have discretion).

question: How is a five-second penalty served and how are competitors told about it?
reference: The stewards give written notification to the competitor and inform all competitors via the OMS; the driver stops in the designated pit stop position for the penalty time (Articles B1.9.5 and B1.9.6).

question: Under what circumstances is overtaking allowed during the formation lap behind the Safety Car?
reference: Only in limited cases, for example when a car is delayed leaving the grid, when several cars start from the pit lane and one is delayed, or when a car slows with an obvious problem (Article B5.10.6).

question: What must drivers do during a Virtual Safety Car period?
reference: No car may be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically or dangerously, and all cars must reduce speed and stay above the minimum time set by the FIA ECU in each marshalling sector (Article B5.12.2).

question: How closely must the cars follow the Safety Car when it is deployed?
reference: Cars must form a queue behind the Safety Car no more than ten car lengths apart (Article B5.13.2).

question: How many engines may a driver use in a season under the 2026 sporting regulations?
reference: No more than 3 engines (ICE), 3 turbochargers and the other limited PU elements listed (Article B8.2.2).

question: How are cars weighed after qualifying under the 2026 regulations?
reference: The driver proceeds directly to the FIA garage and stops the engine, and is weighed by the Technical Delegate (Article B3.2.1).

question: When does the first restricted period start relative to the start of FP1?
reference: Restricted Period One starts 42 hours before the scheduled start of FP1 and ends 29 hours before it (Article B9.5.1).

question: How is the classification of a free practice session determined?
reference: By the fastest lap time each driver sets; only laps started and completed by crossing the Control Line on track, not in the pit lane, count (Article B2.1.3).

question: What happens if team personnel are still touching a car on the grid after the fifteen-second signal?
reference: The driver must start from the pit lane, and a Stop-and-Go Penalty is imposed on a driver who fails to start from the pit lane (Article B5.5.5).

question: What is the pit lane speed limit and what is the fine for exceeding it in practice or qualifying?
reference: The limit is 80 km/h (the Race Director may amend it); exceeding it in free practice or qualifying is fined 100 euros per km/h above the limit (Article B1.6.3).

question: Is a driver allowed to drive slowly or erratically on the circuit?
reference: No: an F1 car may not be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically or in a potentially dangerous manner at any time (Article B1.8.5).

question: How are the top ten qualifying positions allocated?
reference: To the drivers who took part in Q3 in order of their best Q3 time (Article B2.4.3).

question: Can a car that did not reach the grid under its own power after the reconnaissance lap still start from the grid?
reference: No: such a car will not be permitted to start from the grid (Article B5.2.4).

question: Which tyres may a driver use during a competition?
reference: Only the sets allocated and made available to that driver as defined in the tyre allocation articles (Article B6.3.1).

question: What happens when the Race Director asks cars to use the pit lane during a Safety Car deployment?
reference: All cars must enter the pit lane, drive through it and re-join the track (Article B5.13.3).

question: What condition must cars meet after the third red light at a standing start?
reference: They must be stationary in their allocated grid position until the start signal is given by extinguishing all red lights (Article B5.11.1).

question: When is a driver judged to have left the track?
reference: When no part of the car remains in contact with the track; white lines are part of the track but kerbs are not (Article B1.8.6).

question: What penalties can stewards impose under the 2022 sporting regulations?
reference: A five-second or ten-second time penalty, a drive-through, and the other penalties listed (Article 54.3).

question: Under the 2022 regulations, when is a driver penalised for an incident?
reference: At the stewards' discretion, and no penalty unless a driver was wholly or predominantly to blame (Article 54.2).

question: In 2022, what message is sent when the safety car is called in?
reference: SAFETY CAR IN THIS LAP is sent via the official messaging system and the car's orange lights are extinguished (Article 55.14).

question: What is signalled when a rolling start is declared under the 2022 regulations?
reference: The message ROLLING START is sent to all competitors, FIA light panels display RS and the safety car's orange lights go out (Article 52.1).

question: How many engines could a driver use in a season in the 2022 sporting regulations?
reference: Three engines (ICE), three MGU-H, three turbochargers, two energy stores and so on (Article 28.2).

question: Where is refuelling permitted according to the 2022 sporting regulations?
reference: Only in the competitors' designated garages (Article 36.1).

question: What does Article 33 of the 2022 sporting regulations require of drivers?
reference: Drive alone and unaided, observe the Code's driving behaviour provisions and make every reasonable effort to use the track (Article 33).

question: How much warning is given before a suspended race is resumed in 2022?
reference: At least ten minutes warning, with signals at ten, five, three and one minute and fifteen seconds before the resumption (Articles 58.1, 58.2).

question: How are cars weighed after free practice or qualifying under the 2022 sporting regulations?
reference: The driver goes straight to the FIA garage and stops the engine when signalled (Article 35.1).

question: In the 2022 regulations, what message goes out when the safety car is deployed?
reference: SAFETY CAR DEPLOYED is sent, FIA light panels show SC and marshals display waved yellow flags and SC boards (Article 55.4).

question: How many engines may a driver use in a season under the 2025 sporting regulations?
reference: Four engines (ICE), four MGU-H, four turbochargers, two energy stores and so on (Article 28.2).

question: How many engines may a driver use in a season under the 2024 sporting regulations?
reference: Four engines (ICE), four MGU-H, four turbochargers and so on (Article 28.2).

question: What penalty applies for a false start in the 2025 sporting regulations?
reference: The penalties in Articles 54.3a), b) or c) are imposed on a driver who moves after the four-second light and before the start signal (Article 48.1).

question: How must cars form up behind the safety car under the 2024 sporting regulations?
reference: They must reduce speed and form up in line behind the safety car no more than ten car lengths apart (Article 55.7).

question: What does the 2025 sporting regulation say about driving slowly while the safety car is deployed?
reference: No car may be driven unnecessarily slowly, erratically or dangerously while the safety car is deployed, on track, pit entry or pit lane (Article 55.5).

question: When does the pit exit open before the formation lap in the 2025 regulations?
reference: Forty minutes before the scheduled start of the formation lap (Article 44.1).

question: How is the starting grid of the race determined in the 2024 sporting regulations?
reference: By the results of the qualifying session (and the sprint session if scheduled) (Article 39.1).

question: What do the 2025 sporting regulations say about leaving the track?
reference: Drivers must make every reasonable effort to use the track and may not leave it without a justifiable reason; white lines are part of the track, kerbs are not (Article 33.3).

question: What is the minimum mass of an F1 car in the 2025 technical regulations?
reference: 800 kg without fuel plus the Heat Hazard Mass Increase (Article 4.1).

question: What is the minimum mass of an F1 car in the 2023 technical regulations?
reference: 798 kg without fuel (Article 4.1).

question: What engine capacity is permitted in the 2025 technical regulations?
What is the maximum fuel mass flow allowed in 2025?
reference: 100 kg/h (Article 5.2.3).

question: How many forward gears must a 2025 car have?
reference: Eight forward gear ratios; continuously variable transmissions are not permitted (Article 9.7.1).

question: Must a car be able to reverse in the 2025 technical regulations?
reference: Yes, all cars must be able to be driven in reverse by the driver at any time during the Competition (Article 9.8).

question: What are the tyre width limits for the front and rear in the 2023 technical regulations?
reference: Between 345 mm and 375 mm at the front and between 440 mm and 470 mm at the rear (Article 10.8.1).

question: How many rear lights must a 2025 car have?
reference: Three rear lights, supplied by FIA designated manufacturers, clearly visible and switchable by the driver (Article 14.3.1).

question: Are automatic gear changes allowed under the 2025 technical regulations?
reference: No, automatic gear changes are considered a driver aid and are not permitted (Article 9.9.1).

question: What is the rule for fitting ballast in 2025?
reference: Ballast must be secured so tools are required to remove it and it stays immobile relative to the sprung mass (Article 4.4).

question: How is the reference mass of the driver established under the 2025 technical regulations?
reference: By the FIA technical delegate at the first Competition of the Championship, and it may be amended during the season (Article 4.6.1).

question: What front and rear axle mass distribution is required in 2025 qualifying?
reference: At least 0.446 and 0.539 of the minimum mass respectively at the front and rear axles (Article 4.2).

question: How many clutch paddles are allowed on the steering wheel in 2025?
reference: A maximum of two, mounted on the steering wheel (Article 9.3.1).

question: What are the requirements for the driver radio in the 2025 technical regulations?
reference: All cars must have a voice radio communication system made by the FIA designated supplier to an FIA specification (Article 8.9.1).

question: How cold may the fuel in a car be when it is running on track in 2025?
reference: Not colder than the lower of ten degrees below ambient temperature or ten degrees centigrade (Article 6.4.2).
